The memorandum aims to facilitate the exchange of information and expertise in the field of occupational safety and health. 4. 5. 6. 7. The document was authored by Dr. Björn Arvidson. Introduction 8. Ethyl ether is a colorless, highly volatile liquid with a characteristic pungent odor. 9. It poses a significant fire hazard as its vapor readily forms explosive mixtures with air and oxygen. 10. Ethyl ether is miscible with lower aliphatic alcohols, benzene, chloroform, petroleum ether, other fat solvents, and many oils. 11. The primary physiological effect of ethyl ether is general anesthesia. Chemical Properties and Hazards 12. Ethyl ether begins to oxidize shortly after distillation, forming ether peroxides, acetaldehyde, and acetic acid. 13. Ether peroxide is less volatile than ethyl ether and tends to concentrate during evaporation or distillation. 14. Concentrated ether peroxides present a serious detonation hazard. 15. Testing for peroxides in ethyl ether can be performed by shaking 10 mL of ether with 1 mL of a freshly prepared 10% aqueous potassium iodide solution in a light-protected glass cylinder. A yellow color indicates the presence of peroxides. 16. Peroxides can be removed by distillation or by passing the ether through an alumina column. Activated alumina also dries the ether during this process. 17. Ferrous sulfate (30% solution in water) can be used to extract and destroy peroxides in ethyl ether. Storage and Stability 18. Factors that delay the decomposition of ethyl ether include the absence of light, storage in a cool place, and storage in copper tanks or contact with copper screens. 19. Copper and certain other metals, such as iron and mercury, prevent the oxidation of ethyl ether by preferentially oxidizing and consuming the oxygen that would otherwise combine with ethyl ether. 20. Ethyl ether should be stored in its original metal cans rather than in glass bottles. 21. Very dry ethyl ether oxidizes more readily than ether containing small amounts of water. Production and Uses 22. Ethyl ether is produced on a large scale by dehydrating ethanol or hydrating ethylene, both processes involving sulfuric acid. 23. It is widely used in the chemical industry as a solvent for fats, oils, dyes, gums, resins, raw rubber, smokeless powder, perfumes, and nitrocellulose. 24. Ethyl ether is also used in the manufacture of photographic films, pharmaceuticals, and as a reaction and extraction medium in the chemical industry. 25. Additionally, it serves as an inhalation anesthetic in surgery, a refrigerant, a component in diesel fuels, a cleaning agent in dry cleaning, and a starting fuel for engines. 27. 28. Analytical Methods 29. Ethyl ether in air can be analyzed using charcoal tube sampling followed by gas chromatography. 30. 31. Breath samples can be analyzed by direct injection into a gas chromatograph, with calculations based on standard curves. Distribution and Metabolism 32. After inhalation, ethyl ether is rapidly absorbed from alveoli into the blood, with no barrier posed by the alveolar membrane. 33. The blood/gas distribution coefficient of ethyl ether is high, leading to slow induction of anesthesia. 34. Approximately 8-10% of absorbed ethyl ether is metabolized in the body, primarily by hepatic microsomal enzymes, while the remainder is exhaled unchanged. 35. Metabolism produces ethanol and acetaldehyde, which are further oxidized to acetate and enter intermediary metabolism. Toxicity and Effects 36. 37. 38. 39. Ethyl ether has complex effects on learning and memory in experimental studies, with some reports of retrograde amnesia. Elimination 40. Elimination of ethyl ether from fatty tissues occurs slowly, taking approximately 8 hours. 41. Termination of anesthesia with ethyl ether is slower in obese individuals due to partitioning into body fat. Mechanism of Action 42. The exact mechanism by which ethyl ether produces anesthesia remains unclear, but it likely involves interactions with membrane lipids or hydrophobic regions of membrane-bound proteins. 43. Some evidence suggests that the GABA receptor may be a target for inhalation anesthetics like ethyl ether. Conclusion 44.
